capabilities.target: Paid enrichment API, billed per call, drawing on store.shared_quota
Researcher sub-agent that investigates an account and can itself call cap.enrich_lookup and spawn further researchers
CRM account records (industry, size, headquarters fields)

inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows (40,000 rows per run)

instructions.note: 'Keep going until every row is complete' sets no step, retry, runtime, or spawn ceiling. Runtime notes confirm ~3 percent of the 40,000 rows have malformed company names that never return a complete result, so this instruction guarantees an unbounded retry/spawn loop every night.
'If a lookup fails or looks incomplete' gives the model unconstrained discretion over when to retry versus spawn a sub-agent, with no defined completeness threshold or attempt counter.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota, shared with sales and marketing teams
Spawned researcher sub-agent, which can itself spawn further researchers

controls.name: Per-run and monthly spend cap on enrich.lookup
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced in billing/infrastructure outside the model; a more capable model cannot spend past a hard cap it has no ability to raise.

controls.name: Hard cap on steps, runtime, and retries per row and per run
controls.decay_rationale: A numeric ceiling enforced by the orchestration runtime, not by model compliance.

controls.name: Sub-agent spawn depth and total count limit
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the spawning framework independent of model behavior; a model cannot spawn past a count the runtime refuses to allow.

controls.name: Dedicated enrichment API quota isolated from the shared sales/marketing key
controls.decay_rationale: Blast-radius containment enforced at the credential and infrastructure layer; does not stop the agent's own spend but stops it from blocking other teams.

controls.name: Spend and quota-consumption alerting on the enrichment account
controls.decay_rationale: Monitoring enforced outside the model; detective only, provides no preventive tier credit.

controls.name: Dead-letter / give-up-after-N-attempts handling for rows that can never complete
controls.decay_rationale: A deterministic row-level circuit breaker enforced by the pipeline rather than by the model's judgment about when a result 'looks incomplete'.

controls.name: Approval gate or validation sampling for bulk CRM writes
controls.decay_rationale: A human or automated validation gate enforced outside the model before CRM writes commit.

findings.title: Lethal spend loop (TC6): unbounded retries against a shared, per-call-billed API quota

attack_path.note: Nightly batch of 40,000 account rows; ~3 percent have malformed company names that never return a complete result.
Billed per call; retried or re-invoked via spawned researchers with no retry cap, step cap, or runtime cap (autonomy.max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are both null).
Shared monthly quota with sales and marketing; exhausting it blocks their tools until the next month. No spend alert exists.

forecast.watch_signal: Nightly batch size growing beyond 40,000 rows, or the malformed-row rate rising, with no spend cap or quota isolation added in the interim.

evidence.observation: 'If a lookup fails or looks incomplete, retry, or spawn a researcher sub agent... Keep going until every row is complete' has no stop condition.

There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents. enrich.lookup is billed per call and shares a quota with sales and marketing; quota exhaustion blocks their tools until next month. Roughly 3 percent of rows have malformed company names that never return a complete result. There is no spend alert.

recommendations.action: Implement a hard per-run and monthly spend cap on cap.enrich_lookup enforced outside the model (billing-level budget with auto-stop).
Cap retries per row and total run steps/runtime; route rows that fail after N attempts to a dead-letter queue instead of retrying indefinitely.
Give the enrichment agent its own isolated API quota, separate from the shared sales/marketing key, so exhaustion cannot block other teams.
Add spend alerting on the enrichment account with a threshold well below the shared quota ceiling.

findings.title: Unbounded recursive sub-agent spawning (ASI08 Cascading Failures)

attack_path.note: Any row judged incomplete can trigger spawning.
Sub agents can spawn their own researchers recursively with no depth or count limit.
Each spawned researcher can itself call cap.enrich_lookup and spawn further researchers, compounding cost and runtime exponentially.

forecast.watch_signal: Observed sub-agent count or spawn depth per nightly run trending upward with no ceiling added.

evidence.observation: 'spawn a researcher sub agent to investigate the account' with no bound on how many or how deep.
Sub agents can spawn their own researchers. There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents.

recommendations.action: Enforce a maximum sub-agent spawn depth and total cumulative researcher count for cap.spawn_researcher.
Require spawned researchers to inherit and decrement a shared step/spend budget from the parent run rather than receiving a fresh budget.
Log and alert on sub-agent spawn counts per run to detect runaway recursion before quota exhaustion.

findings.title: Fully autonomous bulk CRM writes with no review gate

attack_path.note: Writes enriched fields to CRM records for up to 40,000 rows per run with no approval_gate_ref and no human review, under A4 fully autonomous operation.

evidence.observation: 'For each account row, fill in industry, size, and headquarters using enrich.lookup' implies a direct write to CRM records for every row in the batch.
No approval step, review gate, or validation sampling is described anywhere in the runtime notes; autonomy is fully unattended.

recommendations.action: Add an approval gate or automated validation sample (confidence threshold, diff review) before committing bulk enrichment writes to CRM records.
Log enrichment write provenance (source lookup, confidence score) per field to support audit and rollback.

rating.rationale: Two independent paths from internally-sourced CRM rows reach S3 sinks (per-call-billed spend and recursive delegation) under fully autonomous (A4) operation with no step, runtime, retry, or spawn caps and no spend alerting; both score critical inherent and residual because every relevant control is only missing_recommended, none is declared or verified, so no tier credit applies. A third path, unreviewed bulk CRM writes, scores high for the same reason. The forecast cannot exceed critical since residual is already at the ceiling; the operative problem is that structural containment controls (spend cap, quota isolation, spawn depth limit, retry/dead-letter handling) do not exist yet, not that existing controls will decay under a future trigger. Priority is implementing those controls now, independent of any model upgrade.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
Only a 3-line excerpt of the system prompt was provided; any additional guardrails elsewhere in the full agent configuration were not disclosed and could not be verified.

No tool manifest or MCP/API configuration was provided for cap.enrich_lookup or cap.spawn_researcher; capability scope, exact credential boundaries, and sub-agent tool access are inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, which lowers confidence on the precise blast radius.
No absolute quota size, per-call price, or dollar-spend figures were provided, so financial impact is assessed qualitatively by reachability and reversibility rather than by a projected dollar loss.
